texts: Thymomas are classified by their histology (the WHO types) and staged by their invasion (Masaoka), not by their size.
Large, invasive malignant thymomas can be treated first with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, with or without radiotherapy, to make complete resection possible: C is the answer.
Myasthenia gravis does not worsen the outcome, debulking is not the mainstay, and the diagnosis is made by core or surgical biopsy rather than fine-needle aspiration.
